summary: Compares the authors' Timeless pipeline (two-pass gpt-4o-mini prompting that first groups requirements into epics, then emits JSON-constrained Gherkin and fills coverage gaps) against a two-sentence zero-shot prompt on four PURE requirements documents (107 requirements). Measures structural validity, TF-IDF and embedding-based requirement coverage, and a pre-registered blind rating by four external SE researchers.

claims.claim: JSON-constrained pipeline yields 100% structurally valid scenarios vs 99% for baseline
claims.evidence: Table 2 / §4.3 RQ1: 0 invalid of 119 Timeless scenarios; baseline has one mal-ordered scenario in Gamma-J. Margin is a single scenario; validity is guaranteed by construction (schema + post-validation).

claims.claim: Semantic requirement coverage is comparable (94.3% vs 92.9%)
claims.evidence: Table 3 / §4.3 RQ2. Four documents, single run each; embedding model text-embedding-3-small is from the same provider as the generator, which the authors flag as a possible inflation. Baseline wins negative-scenario coverage (81.2% vs 67.0%) and TF-IDF RCR (76.0% vs 72.0%).

claims.claim: Experts prefer epic-organized Gherkin on Correctness (4.61 vs 4.14), Executability (4.61 vs 4.07), Completeness (4.31 vs 3.50)
claims.evidence: Table 4 matches abstract numbers. Pre-registered on OSF, blinded A/B assignment, 4 raters from independent organizations. But Fleiss' kappa is -0.08 to 0.03 (no agreement), Completeness is one rating per rater per document (n=16 ratings per system), no significance test reported, and H3 was falsified (Completeness went the other way).

claims.claim: Lexical TF-IDF metrics underestimate coverage of abstracted Gherkin
claims.evidence: Fig. 3b: CCTNS 44% lexical vs 96% semantic for Timeless; plausible but rests on the unvalidated embedding threshold.

patterns.note: Structured, schema-constrained acceptance criteria rated more executable/correct than free-form, on small evidence.
Generates BDD specs from requirements; quality gains vs a strawman, coverage equal, negative scenarios worse.
Gherkin is a test-first artifact but no step definitions or executable tests are produced or run.
Two-pass plan (epic synthesis) then generate/gap-fill; no ablation of the two passes separately.

methodology.sample: 4 PURE SRS documents (KeePass, Gamma-J, CCTNS, Internet Peering), 107 requirements, 119 Timeless scenarios; 4 expert raters
methodology.baselines: Two-sentence zero-shot prompt with same model; authors concede few-shot or CoT baselines would narrow gaps (§6 internal validity)
methodology.models: gpt-4o-mini only (generation); text-embedding-3-small for semantic coverage
methodology.variance: Single run per document; Fleiss' kappa near zero; no CIs or tests
methodology.ablations: None separating epic grouping, JSON schema, and gap-fill pass
methodology.contamination_controls: None; PURE is a public dataset
methodology.languages: English natural-language requirements to Gherkin; no code

standards.peer_review: Accepted at SEET 2026 (Springer proceedings) per arXiv comment
standards.artifacts: Evaluation materials and analysis scripts on OSF (osf.io/9apdf); Timeless pipeline code release not stated
standards.preregistration: Expert evaluation pre-registered on OSF with hypotheses H1-H3

biases.detail: Two-sentence zero-shot prompt with no schema, examples or BDD constraints; authors themselves frame result as structured vs unstructured prompting.
Four documents, 107 requirements, four raters; authors note four data points per metric are not enough for statistical generalization.
Only gpt-4o-mini; single run per document.
No repeated runs, no significance tests; inter-rater kappa is approximately zero.
Timeless is the authors' own platform [15]; mitigated by blinded external raters.
Semantic coverage uses an embedding model from the same provider as the generator, with no human-validated threshold.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Authors' own research platform Timeless; OpenAI models used, not evaluated
coi.funding: FAST doctoral network (Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture) and ANSE (1822/31/2025)
coi.detail: Academic authors evaluating their own research tool favorably; no commercial vendor, and rating was blinded and done by non-authors.

verdict_reason: Peer-reviewed and has a pre-registered blinded rating, but the comparison is against a strawman zero-shot prompt, with one model, one run, four documents and near-zero rater agreement. Coverage parity and the structural guarantee are the only robust takeaways.
applicability: Relevant to spec-driven rollout: if the team drafts acceptance criteria for service features with an LLM, use a JSON schema plus a deterministic validator so Gherkin is always well-formed, and check coverage with more than one metric. Do not read this as evidence that epic-grouping beats per-requirement generation for domain content rules; the baseline is weak, negative-scenario coverage dropped (81% to 67%), which matters for validation/error paths in cross-repository work, and nothing tests whether the Gherkin compiles into Cucumber-JVM step definitions across the team's several repositories. Host-neutral: the technique is a prompt + schema, portable across agent hosts.
